# 2 Samuel 24 — Disagreement Log
**Chapter:** 2 Samuel 24 (25 verses)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA
**Total disagreements logged:** 10

---

## V.1 — "incited" vs. "stirred up"
- **EMET/LOGOS:** "incited" (*vayyaset*)
- **PNEUMA:** "stirred up"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "incited." More precise rendering of *vayyaset*; "stirred up" softens the theological difficulty.

---

## V.3 — "desire this thing" vs. "why on earth... want to do this"
- **EMET/LOGOS:** "why does my lord the king desire this thing?"
- **PNEUMA:** "why on earth does my lord the king want to do this?"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "why does my lord the king desire this thing?" Formal address appropriate for Joab to king.

---

## V.10 — "David's heart struck him" vs. "stricken with guilt"
- **EMET/LOGOS:** "David's heart struck him"
- **PNEUMA:** "David was stricken with guilt"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "David's heart struck him." Preserves the remarkable Hebrew idiom of conscience as physical blow.

---

## V.10 — "acted very foolishly" vs. "been an utter fool"
- **EMET:** "I-have-been-very-foolish"
- **LOGOS:** "I have acted very foolishly"
- **PNEUMA:** "I have been an utter fool"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "I have acted very foolishly." LOGOS captures the verbal form *niskalti* while maintaining register.

---

## V.13 — "know and see" vs. "consider and decide" vs. "think it over"
- **EMET:** "know and-see"
- **LOGOS:** "consider and decide"
- **PNEUMA:** "think it over"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "consider and decide." LOGOS balances the two Hebrew imperatives naturally.

---

## V.14 — "I am in great distress" vs. "this is agonizing"
- **EMET/LOGOS:** "I am in great distress"
- **PNEUMA:** "This is agonizing"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "I am in great distress." Closer to the Hebrew *tsar-li me'od*.

---

## V.16 — "relented" vs. "was grieved"
- **EMET/LOGOS:** "relented"
- **PNEUMA:** "was grieved"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "relented." Standard translation of *vayyinnachem* in this context; conveys the change in action.

---

## V.17 — "the flock/sheep" rendering
- **EMET:** "the-flock [ha-tson]"
- **LOGOS:** "these, the sheep"
- **PNEUMA:** "they are just sheep"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "these, the sheep." Preserves Hebrew demonstrative structure without PNEUMA's added diminutive.

---

## V.24 — "buying I will buy" vs. "I will buy for a price" vs. "I insist on paying"
- **EMET:** "buying I-will-buy [qanoh eqneh]"
- **LOGOS:** "I will buy it from you for a price"
- **PNEUMA:** "I insist on paying you a fair price"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "I will buy it from you for a price." LOGOS renders the infinitive absolute emphasis through the prepositional phrase.

---

## V.25 — "was entreated" vs. "answered the prayers"
- **EMET/LOGOS:** "was entreated" (*vaye'ater*)
- **PNEUMA:** "answered the prayers"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "was entreated." Preserves the Hebrew passive construction.

---
*— SOPHIA*
